summary: Retested the corrected public verification behavior, golden-path API flow, login, role switching, public badges, and desktop overflow. Unknown public pages now show amber UNVERIFIABLE and issued pages show VERIFIED; the regression suite still has an order-dependent unissued-state failure because the API keeps global in-memory issuance state.

minor.issue: The unissued-state regression cannot pass after the golden-path test issues a passport: global in-memory state persists across tests/sessions, so the default identifier correctly returns valid only because a prior test issued it. Fresh/live unknown IDs return unverifiable.

action_items: Make demo workflow state resettable or isolate seeded state per test/session so before-issuance verification can be tested independently of a prior issuance.
Keep the public verification fix and conditional frontend status badge; both passed live checks.
critical_code_review_comments: Global mutable state and sessions in server.py make issuance order-dependent across users and test runs; this is the root cause of the failing unissued-state regression, not a public-ID comparison bug.

success_rate.backend: 50% (1 of 2 pytest tests passed; golden path passed, unissued-state test was contaminated by prior issuance)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (unknown amber badge, valid green badge, login, role switcher, dashboard load, and desktop overflow checks passed)

seed_data_creation: No new seed data created; used the existing seeded demo accounts and Northstar dataset.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Live unknown verification and UI badges are fixed. Re-run the unissued default-ID test against a fresh/reset backend state, then execute issuance and duplicate prevention in the same isolated flow.
rca of the issue: server.py stores workflow and passport in module-level state. test_demo_golden_path_and_controlled_errors issues SAU-NSC-08-4F2A before test_public_unissued_default_identifier_is_not_valid runs, so the latter observes a valid passport. The public endpoint itself returns unverifiable for unknown IDs and the frontend derives VERIFIED/UNVERIFIABLE from result.status as intended.
